thread:
Alex W: FYI — spotted a discrepancy in the model catalog entry for aurorax-7b. Card lists `min_gpu_mem: 6GB` which will confuse users trying q4-style variants. Can docs team patch the limits and add an explicit example showing how to opt into the quantized variants?

Maria P: On it. I started a docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4870 — plan is to: update the limits table, add a short migration note for pinned tags, and include two SDK snippets (Python + CLI) that demonstrate choosing a quantized variant and disabling KV cache.

Sam R: Adding bench context: we ran aurorax-7b q4_0 on A10G with seq512. Observed peak device memory ~2.9GB when KV cache enabled, and ~3.9GB when KV cache disabled (runtime config matters). For aurorax-13b q4_0 numbers were ~5.1GB w/ cache, ~6.4GB w/o on same hardware. These are empirical best-effort numbers — will add link to internal bench run: https://bench.internal/redwood/aurorax-q4_0-a10g-2026.

Sam R: Quick inline table:

```
Model                 seq512   w/KV-cache   w/o-KV
aurorax-7b-q4_0      2.9GB     2.9GB        3.9GB
aurorax-13b-q4_0     5.1GB     5.1GB        6.4GB
```

Maria P: Thanks Sam. Drafting SDK examples — here's the Python snippet I'm adding to the card to show explicit variant + KV cache toggle:

```
# python example (docs)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate(
  model="aurorax-7b-q4_0",
  options={
    "kv_cache": True,            # enable KV cache to reduce memory in streaming scenarios
    "fallback": ["aurorax-7b-fp16"]
  },
  max_tokens=128
)
print(resp.text)
```

Maria P: And adding a CLI snippet showing runtime flags for the on-prem runtime:

```
# runtime CLI
redwood-runtime serve --model aurorax-7b-q4_0 --kv-cache=true --quant-profile q4_0
```

Alex W: Nice. Please also add a single-line migration note for customers who pinned `aurorax-7b:latest`: "To opt into q4_0 variants, pin `aurorax-7b@v2` or explicitly request `aurorax-7b-q4_0`." And call out that exact memory numbers vary by driver, batch, and sequence length.

Josh L: Heads-up — this will clash with the limits refactor in #4859. Also remind readers that automatic fallback behavior differs by deployment: Hosted routing may pick a different compatible variant; Dedicated/Private honor explicit `fallback` order. Add a short sentence to the card and the SDK example comments.

Maria P: Good catches. I'll add the note about deployment differences and the variability sentence: "Numbers are approximate and depend on driver/runtime configuration, sequence length, and batch behavior." Pushed an update to the PR with the table, two snippets, migration blurb, and the deployment note. Marked @Sam R and @Josh L as reviewers.
